content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I recently purchased [product_name] [version_no] DVD from [company_name]. I installed it on Windows 7 without issues and updated to [version_no]. All my projects from the demo version work fine. My setup involves running Windows 7 on a MacBook Pro using BootCamp with Parallels Desktop, and the software also works when installed on the Mac OSX partition. However, I'm facing trouble updating the software online—it fails. I downloaded the update zip to [version_no] from [company_name]'s update page, but when running the 'Setup' update, it reports an error stating the installer is damaged and should be trashed. Has anyone else encountered this issue or found a solution? Currently, I can run [version_no] on Windows and [version_no] on Mac. I'm concerned it might be a Yosemite-specific problem. Has anyone managed to run [version_no] (not demo) on Mavericks, the previous Mac OS? It would be helpful to have [version_no] running on Mac to access reference files more easily instead of switching screens. Any suggestions or fixes would be greatly appreciated. Thank you, [user_name]
I can confirm that [product_name] [version_no] works perfectly on OSX Yosemite, and the update from [version_no] to [version_no] went smoothly for me.
When I try to update to [product_name] [version_no], the setup.zip downloads correctly, but it doesn't install in Yosemite (Dutch language OS).

After installing the update to [version_no] in Yosemite, ensure you have the correct Java version installed on your MacBook. You can download the Java installer from Apple's page: [url]. Install it, restart your system, and then try running [version_no] again.

Thank you for the updates. I tried the Java installer from the provided link, but it only installed an older Java version for Mac, which didn't solve the issue. After further research, I found a solution related to the Java signature. On Mac, open System Preferences, go to Security and Privacy, and select the General tab. Unlock the settings and choose 'Allow apps to be downloaded from: Anywhere.' Then run the downloaded upgrade to [version_no], and it will prompt you to locate your original licensed version folder. Select the correct folder, and the update should proceed. After restoring my security settings and rebooting, everything works fine now. Thanks for everyone's help, [user_name]

Hi, On my MacBook running OSX Yosemite, [product_name] [version_no] works, but I'm unable to connect to my device using the [product_name]-USB cable. I can't select communication ports like COM 1 or COM 2, as is possible in Windows. This is the only information available. Can anyone assist with this?
A new question by [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread titled Windows 10, [product_name] [version_no] update. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced problems updating [product_name] from [version_no] to [version_no] on MacOS, particularly with installer errors linked to security settings and Java version compatibility. There were also hardware connection issues with the [product_name]-USB cable under MacOS, as communication ports available in Windows were missing, highlighting differences in driver support and hardware compatibility across operating systems.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] [version_no] to be installable and fully operational on MacOS, including straightforward updates, reliable Java compatibility, and seamless hardware connectivity (e.g., [product_name]-USB cable) comparable to the Windows experience.
